record.paper_title: Some open problems about aspherical closed manifolds
record.context_brief: Poincaré duality groups and manifold realization
record.original_question: For a natural number n, is a finitely presented group an n-dimensional Poincaré duality group exactly when it occurs as the fundamental group of an aspherical closed n-dimensional topological manifold?

evidence.quote: A finitely presented group is a n-dimensional Poincare duality group if and only if it is the fundamental group of an aspherical closed n-dimensional topological manifold.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let n be a positive integer. Recall that a group G is called an n-dimensional Poincaré duality group (a PD(n)-group) if it is of type FP, satisfies H^i(G; ZG) = 0 for i ≠ n, and H^n(G; ZG) ≅ Z. A topological space X is aspherical if its higher homotopy groups π_i(X) vanish for all i ≥ 2.

Question: Is it true that, for every positive integer n, a finitely presented group G is an n-dimensional Poincaré duality group if and only if G is isomorphic to the fundamental group of some closed aspherical n-dimensional topological manifold?
artifact.status_search_result: The "only if" direction (the Wall/PD(n) realization problem) is widely regarded as open in general. It is known to hold for n = 2 (Eckmann–Linnell–Müller) and partial results exist for n = 3 (Kropholler–Thomas; further progress via geometrization). For n ≥ 4, Davis constructed PD(n) groups that are not fundamental groups of closed aspherical manifolds in some categories (e.g., groups without finite K(G,1) complexes), and the general realization question remains open and is closely tied to the Borel conjecture. The "if" direction is classical and known.

status_evidence.title: Aspherical manifolds - Manifold Atlas
status_evidence.snippet: It is an open question whether a finitely presented Poincaré duality group is always the fundamental group of a closed aspherical manifold.
status_evidence.claim: The conjecture is open in general; partial results in low dimensions; counterexamples by Davis in higher-dimensional refinements.
